I found the MATCH continuation at that path and checked it alongside the joint note. I’m also testing whether a marked conformal comparison with only first-derivative control can recover the base energy. That would weaken the smooth-convergence hypothesis in the previous result.

The first-derivative argument now gives a conditional result on a whole marked base. With locally bounded curvature in the comparison metric, both chiral Weyl energies converge on each compact, and the smooth limiting metric is Bach-flat. I’ve sent the proof for independent checks, especially the step that turns this local convergence into a statement about the original smooth four-sphere.

There’s now a result on the approximately critical sequence itself. In a positive Ricci representative, I normalized distances by the smallest radius of a ball carrying half the physical Yamabe volume. This keeps physical volume from concentrating at points or escaping to infinity in that gauge. I’m checking how much of that volume reaches regular points of the metric limit, and what would still be needed to turn those points into a marked collar.

**We obtained a physical-volume witness on the approximately critical sequence itself.** For every \(\epsilon,\zeta>0\), after passing to a subsequence, finitely many disjoint smoothly embedded standard four-balls carry at least \(1-\epsilon\) of the physical Yamabe volume. Each ball has physical full-curvature energy below \(\zeta\). The number of balls is independent of the sequence index once the tolerances are fixed. [Derivation](sandbox:/Users/ebbaker/Documents/smooth-poincare-4d/papers/investigations-1/03_first_order_twistor/01_sections_and_connections/02_dirac_collar_extraction/notes/E16_POSITIVE_RICCI_VOLUME_MARKING_20261125.md)

The scale comes from the smallest ball in a conformal positive Ricci metric that carries half the **physical** volume. At this scale the Ricci metrics are noncollapsed, and the physical volume has locally bounded density in their limit. This locates volume at four-dimensional regular points where Cheeger–Colding’s theorem supplies smooth ball embeddings on the original manifolds. The complement of these balls may still carry the chiral energy or the smooth type. genui{"citation":{"refs":["turn782341590view0","turn443245623view1"]}}

**We also weakened what is needed to recover a whole nonround base.** A compatible marking of every punctured truncation now requires local \(C^0\) and strong \(W^{1,4}\) convergence, together with a local scalar-curvature \(L^2\) bound in the comparison gauge. At positive-class minimization, a nonround base satisfying those hypotheses has the original smooth type. The physical metrics converge to it in measured Gromov–Hausdorff distance, with no residual full-curvature energy.

The parallel checks found that matching mean slopes can coexist with a finite negative nonradial end current on shrinking-width round shells. For the closed survivor, the chiral Cotton calculation gives an exact test for a smooth half-harmonic representative. When it exists and the chiral Weyl block is nonzero, that representative is Einstein.

The remaining geometric step is to control first derivatives on the actual ball markings and extend them to a whole nonround base, or to obtain a buffered cut separating both prescribed chiral masses. All three registers and continuation notes are updated. Repository hygiene passed. Live chat capture was unavailable, so only a labeled partial public record was saved.

I’m centering the paper on one inequality. If a spherical cut preserves positive Yamabe sign and leaves a capped piece on the original smooth manifold, the energy discarded by a near-minimizer is bounded by its excess above the infimum plus the cost of capping. This gives the volume-bearing balls a precise role and identifies what still has to be proved about their boundaries.

The 16-page draft is assembled. It gives both the two-sided cut argument and a shorter test for an already parametrized four-ball, whose exterior can be repaired on the same smooth manifold. Created the master investigation directly under `papers/master` and wrote its first manuscript, [**Chiral Weyl energy and the smooth four-dimensional Poincaré conjecture** (PDF, 16 pages)](sandbox:/Users/ebbaker/Documents/smooth-poincare-4d/output/pdf/master/chiral_weyl_energy_and_smooth_poincare.pdf). The [LaTeX source](sandbox:/Users/ebbaker/Documents/smooth-poincare-4d/papers/master/manuscript/chiral_weyl_energy_and_smooth_poincare.tex) is in the new investigation.

The paper retains the shared introduction, from isothermal coordinates and uniformization through four-dimensional twistor geometry. It then develops one argument. On a hypothetical nonstandard smooth homotopy four-sphere, suppose a nearly minimizing positive-Yamabe metric admits a marked spherical cut whose caps preserve positivity and satisfy the stated energy bounds. One capped piece retains the original smooth type. Comparing that piece with the infimum on the **same smooth manifold** bounds the energy discarded by the cut by the minimizing excess plus the capping cost. A sufficiently inexpensive cut carrying definite chiral energy on both sides would therefore give a contradiction.

The volume result sharpens the outstanding question. In the stated range, one can locate disjoint, smoothly parametrized four-balls carrying nearly all the physical volume. The paper derives a one-sided replacement estimate for these balls and identifies what would make it decisive: control of the cost of repairing their boundaries and of the chiral energy on the small-volume complement. Those estimates remain open, as does entry into the required positive-Yamabe energy range on an arbitrary smooth homotopy sphere.
